Ⅰ.하박국 개관\n - 하박국은 스바냐, 예레미야와 동시대 사역자. 바벨:
Ⅰ. Habakkuk Overview
 - Habakkuk ministered at the same time as Zephaniah and Jeremiah. The Babylonian army has come, surrounded Jerusalem, and is killing people and carrying them off. If you've lost the war and you're under siege, what kind of situation is that? It's God's discipline. And the level of discipline is about medium...
우리도 보면 분위기 파악을 못하는 사람 있죠? 지금 하나님께서 화를 참고: You know how some people just can't read the room? God has held back His anger and held it back and held it back, and now He's disciplining them. So what should you do at a time like this? Even taking your beating quietly and repenting wouldn't be enough, but instead he's saying, 'Hold on, You're God, so why are You just sitting there in a situation like this? The wicked are tormenting the righteous, God, is this normal?' That's how he's arguing with God.
<합1:1~4> 선지자 하박국의 묵시로 받은 경고라 여호와여 내가 부르짖: <Hab 1:1~4> The burden which Habakkuk the prophet did see. O LORD, how long shall I cry, and thou wilt not hear! even cry out unto thee of violence, and thou wilt not save! Why dost thou shew me iniquity, and cause me to behold grievance? for spoiling and violence are before me: and there are that raise up strife and contention. Therefore the law is slacked, and judgment doth never go forth: for the wicked doth compass about the righteous; therefore wrong judgment proceedeth.
하박국의 생각에는 악인은 바벨론이고 의인은 예루살렘임. 이런식으로 세계: In Habakkuk's mind, the wicked are Babylon and the righteous are Jerusalem. "If this is how You run world history, of course the law is slacked and judgment is twisted!" He's fuming.
<합1:6~11> 보라 내가 사납고 성급한 백성 곧 땅의 넓은 곳으로 다:
<Hab 1:6~11> For, lo, I raise up the Chaldeans, that bitter and hasty nation, which shall march through the breadth of the land, to possess the dwellingplaces that are not theirs.
 - Habakkuk's cry is: the wicked (Babylon) are surrounding and tormenting the righteous, so why is God silent?
그런데 하나님께서는 ‘그들을 내가 보냈다’고 하는 거예요. 그러면서 “안: But God says, 'I'm the one who sent them.' And then: "I was already planning to kill those guys anyway." Why? Because they tormented you way too much...
하박국 “아니 만세전부터 계신 하나님께서 누가 선하고 악한지 아실 것 아: Habakkuk: "But God, You've been there from everlasting, surely You know who's good and who's evil?"
그러면서 내가 성루에 올라가서 하나님 대답을 들어 보겠다도 호기롭게 말해: And then he boldly says, I'm going to go up on the watchtower and hear what God answers.
2절. 하나님께서 기가차서 대답하십니다. “야, 이 묵시는 정한 때가 있: Verse 2. God is stunned and answers. "Look, this vision has an appointed time. Though it tarry, it will surely come." So until the time God has set, even Babylon gets to strut around. And then: "You keep going on about the righteous, the righteous. If there were any righteous, I'd be looking after them more than you would, my friend."
<합2:4> 보라 그의 마음은 교만하며 그의 속에서 정직하지 못하니라 그: <Hab 2:4> Behold, his soul which is lifted up is not upright in him: but the just shall live by his faith.
The righteous do not die, because of faith.
"Lots of people died today too." "Those weren't righteous either."
그럼 끝난거죠 뭐. 하박국은 자기들은 의인이고 바벨론은 악인이라고 규정하: Then that's it, game over. Habakkuk had decided that they were the righteous and Babylon was the wicked, and he was crying "Save the righteous!", right? But God says there isn't a single righteous person? So what does that mean? It means a Jerusalem with not one righteous person left is no different from Babylon.
그래서 6절에 보면 그 바벨론을 물 자들도 홀연히 일어날 것이다. 실제로: So in verse 6 it says those who will bite Babylon will suddenly rise up. And in fact in B.C. 539 Babylon falls to King Cyrus of Persia.
<합2:14> 대저 물이 바다를 덮음같이 여호와의 영광을 인정하는 것이:
<Hab 2:14> For the earth shall be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD, as the waters cover the sea.
 - So when the nations see mighty Babylon fall, the knowledge of the LORD's glory fills the earth. That has already been fulfilled, right? So the earth being filled with the knowledge of the LORD as the waters cover the sea is not something still to come. That song doesn't fit.
여기까지 듣고 하박국이 부들부들 살이 떨려 옵니다. 하박국이 악인이라고:
When Habakkuk hears all this, he starts shaking all over. Babylon, the one Habakkuk called wicked, is going to fall, but why does it fall? Because it tormented Israel too much.
 - So then it's settled that Israel will be trampled by Babylon, right? When he realizes this, his whole body starts trembling.
 - The prophet's prayer, from chapter 3 verse 2
여호와여 내가 주께 대한 소문을 듣고 놀랐나이다 여호와여 주는 주의 일을:
O LORD, I have heard thy speech, and was afraid: O LORD, revive thy work in the midst of the years, in the midst of the years make known; in wrath remember mercy.
- Thy work? = Babylon and Israel falling. It's a plea: in wrath remember mercy.
<합3:16~18> 내가 들었으므로 내 창자가 흔들렸고 그 목소리로 인하:
<Hab 3:16~18> When I heard, my belly trembled; my lips quivered at the voice: rottenness entered into my bones, and I trembled in myself, that I might rest in the day of trouble: when he cometh up unto the people, he will invade them with his troops. Although the fig tree shall not blossom, neither shall fruit be in the vines; the labour of the olive shall fail, and the fields shall yield no meat; the flock shall be cut off from the fold, and there shall be no herd in the stalls: Yet I will rejoice in the LORD, I will joy in the God of my salvation.
 - So the prophet looks at himself and thinks: maybe I'm not righteous either, and if I keep complaining and grumbling like this, maybe I'll be cast away too.
그래서 내 자신이라도 추슬러야겠다 하면서 덜덜 떨면서 부른 노래가 바로: So he says, at least I need to pull myself together, and the song he sings while trembling all over is this very passage.
